messages:
lena: Heads-up: the quarterly sampling found 3 cross-project KMS grants for a svcacct `analytics-reporter@partner-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com`. Anyone recognize that principal? :warning:
miguel: i pulled the export, looks like two bindings to `projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/analytics/cryptoKeys/report-key` from a partner svcacct. snippet:
```json
{
  "principal": "serviceAccount:analytics-reporter@partner-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com",
  "role": "roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter",
  "resource": "projects/redwood-prod/.../cryptoKeys/report-key"
}
```
rachel: If it's cross-project we should correlate with cloud audit logs before removing. Quick check to run locally: 
`gcloud logging read 'resource.type="kms_crypto_key" AND protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail:"analytics-reporter@*"' --limit 50 --project=redwood-prod | jq .`
That shows Encrypt/Decrypt calls and the originating service (CI, svc, human).
lena: Can someone run that and paste top results? If it's unused, propose we put it in a 7-day TTL quarantine tag rather than immediate permanent revoke so we don't break an in-progress vuln triage or emergency run.
miguel: ran it: two Encrypt events in the last 14 days from a CircleCI agent. Looks like a misconfigured pipeline. I added a temporary label `temp_revoked_by:eng-security` and created a quarantine tag `kms_quarantine:2026-03-28` so automation can auto-expire. Commands I ran:
- audit: `gcloud logging read 'resource.type="kms_crypto_key" AND protoPayload.methodName:"Encrypt" AND protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail:"analytics-reporter@*"' --limit 10 --project=redwood-prod`
- remove binding (temp): `gcloud projects remove-iam-policy-binding redwood-prod --member='serviceAccount:analytics-reporter@partner-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com' --role='roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter'`
- added labels via infra API and noted in ticket  #SEC-7421
rachel: Good call on quarantine. Automation should: 1) detect cross-project KMS binding, 2) run audit query, 3) if usage==0 -> revoke, if usage>0 and owner unknown -> quarantine with TTL and notify infra + oncall. Pseudo: 
```
if is_kms_binding and cross_project:
  events = run_kms_audit(principal)
  if events == 0:
    schedule_revoke()
  else:
    tag_quarantine(ttl=7d)
    notify(infra, oncall)
```
Also add a field in the entitlement export for `exception_reason` so reviewers can surface approved short-lived cross-project grants.
marta: This is exactly the behavior requested in the least-priv playbook draft. A couple additions: - require an `approved_by` field for any cross-project KMS grant to auto-suppress alerts - add a short TTL for all cross-project KMS grants (7 days default) - if the binding was used as part of a vuln triage (CI or human triggered during patching), treat as a special exception and require post-mortem note in incident system
access-review-bot: Created ticket SEC-7421: "cross-project KMS binding: analytics-reporter@partner-prod" and set severity=low, sla=72h.
infra-bot: permissions-scan completed: 3 quarantine tags applied, 0 critical outstanding KMS grants. :white_check_mark:
lena: Action items: 1) miguel to land automation patch that runs the audit query and applies `kms_quarantine` tag when owner missing; 2) rachel to update the quarterly access-review deck with the new KMS handling diagram and sample command lines; 3) marta to add the TTL + exception requirements to the least-priv playbook. Please link PRs here. If any grant is still active at TTL expiry, automation should email the owner and then revoke after another 24h if unclaimed.
miguel: I'll open the PR this afternoon, name `access-review/kms-quarantine-audit` and include unit tests. Quick note on implementation: the audit query can be expensive if run for every principal; we'll batch principals with `last_seen < 90d` and only run detailed queries for cross-project candidates.
rachel: And add a short runbook step for oncall: how to triage when automation quarantines a KMS binding during an active incident (check `protoPayload.requestMetadata.callerIp` and `resource.labels.project_id` to see if it was part of a known mitigation).
lena: Thanks team. Let's close after PRs merged and update the quarterly deck before the exec review. :thumbsup:
